column3: The Hebrew calls on the earth to hear in the third person; BSB addresses it directly with “hear, O earth.”

The Hebrew does not explicitly name “His people” as the subject; BSB supplies that phrase.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “generation” in “generation and generation”; BSB says “long past.”
The Hebrew says “the sons of Israel”; BSB says “the sons of God.”
The Hebrew uses the image of a measuring cord for the inheritance; BSB says “allotted inheritance.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular “him” for the one taken and carried; BSB uses plural “them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “he ate” the field’s produce and describes being made to suck honey; BSB says God “fed him” and “nourished him.”
The Hebrew uses the images of the “fat of wheat kidneys” and the “blood of a grape”; BSB has “the choicest grains of wheat” and “the juice of the finest grapes.”
The Hebrew directly addresses Jeshurun with three singular “you” verbs before returning to “he”; BSB keeps the description in the third person throughout.
The Hebrew says “foreign ones” without an explicit noun “gods”; BSB supplies “gods.”
The Hebrew explicitly names “gods” once and then describes the new arrivals; BSB repeats “gods” for the new arrivals.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they are children “with no faithfulness in them”; BSB says “children of unfaithfulness.”
The Hebrew calls their objects “vanities” without an explicit noun “idols”; BSB specifies “worthless idols.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular “tooth” for the beasts and names creeping things of the dust; BSB has plural “fangs” and specifies “vipers.”
The Hebrew names a virgin and a suckling infant; BSB uses the broader terms “young woman” and “infant.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “our hand is high”; BSB expresses this as “Our own hand has prevailed.”
The Hebrew says “they” without explicitly naming Israel; BSB supplies “Israel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew joins the one and two pursuers with “and”; BSB has “or.”
